segments.text: Hey Kayla, how's your week going so far?
Pretty good, thanks. A little busy, but in a good way. How about you?
Same. Back to back meetings, so I'm glad we get this time. Do you want to start, or should I?
I can start. The search indexing project shipped on Friday, and it's already cut query time by about forty percent.
That's fantastic. I saw the dashboard, and the numbers look great. Congratulations.
Thanks. Honestly, I learned a lot. I'd never worked that closely with the data team before.
I noticed. Several people on that team told me how easy you were to work with.
That's nice to hear. It was a good group.
How are you feeling about workload right now? Last time you mentioned you felt stretched.
Better, actually. Finishing the indexing project took a lot off my plate, but I'm still carrying the old billing bug fixes on top of new work.
Right, those billing fixes have been dragging on. How many are left?
Four. Two are quick, and two need real investigation, probably a few days each.
Let's see if I can find someone to take the two bigger ones. I'll talk to Carlos about that today.
That would help a lot. Thank you.
Of course. Now, I want to talk about growth. You said you were interested in technical leadership.
Yes, I am. I'm not sure I want to manage people yet, but I'd love to lead a project from start to finish.
That's a really reasonable path. Leading the mobile notifications project could be a good first step.
I'd love that. What would it involve?
You'd write the design document, coordinate with two other engineers and a designer, and present progress in the weekly planning meeting.
That sounds exciting and a bit scary. In a good way.
That's usually the right mix. Why don't you draft a one page proposal, and we'll review it together next week?
Sure, I can have that ready by Monday.
Perfect. Is there anything about the team or the process that's frustrating you?
One thing. Code reviews sometimes sit for two or three days, and it slows everything down.
Yes, I've heard that from others too. What would help?
Maybe a rotating reviewer each day, so everybody knows who's responsible for picking up new requests.
I like that. Could you write up a short proposal and post it in the team channel? I'll support it in the next standup.
Okay, I'll post it by Thursday.
Great. One more thing from me. I'd like you to practice presenting at the all hands in November, just a five minute demo of the search work.
Oh, wow. Okay. I think I can do that.
You'll do great. I can help you rehearse the week before if that's useful.
Yes please. I always get nervous before presenting.
Totally normal. We'll practice until it feels natural. Anything else on your mind?
No, I think that covers it. Thanks for making time, Jordan.
Anytime. Enjoy the rest of your week, and let me know if anything comes up.

action_items.task: Ask Carlos to take over the two complex billing bug fixes
Draft a one page proposal for leading the mobile notifications project
Post a rotating code reviewer proposal in the team channel
